query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate during sliding in the high-temperature operating regime are governed by the formation of a stable, single-phase solid solution with a high entropy of mixing.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy coating on a conventional metal substrate
generation.intervention: Variation of the coating composition to alter the entropy of mixing
generation.mechanism: Entropy of mixing stabilizes the solid solution, reducing deformation and improving wear resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance and reduced microscopic deformation with increasing entropy of mixing
generation.uncertainty: Limited understanding of the specific effects of entropy of mixing on wear resistance and deformation in high-entropy alloys

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with varying coating compositions and temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate and microscopic deformation do not decrease with increasing entropy of mixing, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: This paper utilizes in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD) to investigate the high-temperature oxidation behaviour of CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy (HEA). We found that (1) Mn is the major oxide-forming element in both vacuum and air environments, leading to the formation of non-protective oxides that deplete the bulk alloy of Mn; (2) no oxides like Cr 2 O 3 , Fe 2 O 3 , or Fe 3 O 4 were observed during the high-temperature oxidation behaviour of CrMnFeCoNi, which contradicts some previous studies on the isothermal oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi HEA. We also analysed and compared the experimental results with thermodynamic calculations by using ThermoCalc version 2022b software following the CALPHAD method. ThermoCalc predicted spinel oxide in a vacuum environment, along with halite oxides observed in experimental results; also, in an atmospheric environment, it predicted only spinel, indicating the need for further investigation into factors to validate the thermodynamic predictions. Refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs) have excellent mechanical properties, which could make them the substitutes of some superalloys. However, the high melting point of refractory HEAs leads to processing problems when using traditional processing techniques. In this study, a single BCC solid solution of NbMoTaW alloy was formed by selective laser melting (SLM) with a linear energy density of up to 2.83 J/mm. The composition distribution was analyzed, and the element with a lower melting point and lower density showed a negative deviation (no more than 5%) of the molar ratio in the formed alloy. The HEA shows an excellent microstructure, microhardness, and corrosion resistance performance compared with traditional superalloys, making it a new substitute metal with great application prospects in aerospace and energy fields.

High entropy or multi principal element alloys are a promising and relatively young concept for designing alloys. The idea of creating alloys without a single main alloying element opens up a wide space for possible new alloy compositions. High entropy alloys based on refractory metals such as W, Mo, Ta or Nb are of interest for future high temperature applications e.g., in the aerospace or chemical industry. However, producing refractory metal high entropy alloys by conventional metallurgical methods remains challenging. For this reason, the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated in the present work. In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed to avoid an expensive atomization of pre-alloyed powder. It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations.
